clue.text: Bad place to cross river — standard package travels this way

indicators.note: the river letter is set so the rearranged word runs across it, i.e. it goes inside
bad here means scrambled out of shape, so the word place is rearranged

parts.note: a standard can be an upright pole or post

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a river is an awkward spot to ferry a regular parcel over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges PLACE and 'to cross' puts R (river) inside it, giving PARCEL. 'Standard' is not the usual quality here but an upright pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcel post is the postal service for sending packages, so a package goes by this route.

clue.text: Wide-ranging Italian sport

definitions.meaning: Marco ..., the Venetian traveller who journeyed as far as China
a game played on horseback with mallets

explanation.surface: An Italian sport that covers a lot of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was a famously far-travelling Venetian, and polo is a mounted ball game.

clue.text: Diet soldiers left unfinished

indicators.note: the word for the soldiers is left without its final letter

parts.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops abandoning their diet halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left unfinished' drops the last T from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of eating or treatment, much like a diet plan.

clue.text: Intimate former partner's heading for ban from services

indicators.note: the former partner's piece goes at the head, in front of the other piece

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to intimate is to make known, to communicate

explanation.surface: An ex-partner's hint that someone is barred from church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like an adjective about closeness but is the verb meaning to make known.
explanation.definitionFit: To excommunicate is to exclude someone from the sacraments and worship of the church.

clue.text: Frequency when contracted office worker will appear

definitions.text: Frequency when contracted office worker will appear

parts.words: Frequency when contracted office worker will appear
parts.note: the answer means once a year, and its abbreviation p.a. is also a PA, a personal assistant in an office

explanation.surface: How often a contract worker will turn up at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' means abbreviated: the Latin phrase shortens to p.a., which also stands for a personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means each year, a frequency of once annually, as in a salary quoted yearly.

clue.text: 'Express' really go-ahead

parts.note: to express something is to say it
so, as in 'it is so', means truly or really

explanation.surface: An express train really has the go-ahead to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their authorising permission, the green light to proceed.

clue.text: Second person appearing in Bible

parts.note: the old singular 'you' pronoun found throughout the King James Bible, read as a character second in line

explanation.surface: Someone asks who the second character in the Bible story is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' suggests a figure such as Eve, but it is the grammatical second person.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic objective form of 'you' singular, used in biblical and prayer language.

clue.text: Bears eating finished jams

indicators.note: the word for bears takes in the word for finished, as if eating it

parts.note: to bear a weight is to hold it
up, as in 'time is up', means finished

explanation.surface: Bears scoffing the last of the jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jams' is not preserves but traffic delays, and 'Bears' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold-ups are traffic delays, the same as jams on the road.

clue.text: Uniform passed — just

parts.note: uniform means level or regular, even
to pass something across is to hand it over

explanation.surface: A uniform was passed over, and only just.
explanation.definitionFit: Being even-handed means treating all sides fairly, which is what a just person does.

clue.text: Record set by one Conservative making sense

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for the UK Conservative party

explanation.surface: A record-setting Conservative politician talking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, what we mean when something makes sense.

clue.text: Shade next door to Anne maybe is down

indicators.note: the royal piece sits right beside the following piece

parts.note: Princess Anne, the King's sister, is an example of a royal
down means sad, blue

explanation.surface: The neighbour of someone called Anne is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne is Princess Anne, a member of the British royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, bright colour, one shade of blue.

clue.text: Dance style that combines ancient and modern modes of expression?

parts.note: Latin is the classic ancient language
American English is a modern variety of the language

explanation.surface: A dance that fuses old and new ways of moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modes of expression' covers both: languages, one ancient and one modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin American is a category of ballroom dance, including the samba, rumba and cha-cha.

clue.text: Second in reality showdown

parts.note: a second is a moment, a brief instant
of here plays the role of in, as in 'a moment in time' versus 'a moment of time'
the truth is what is real

explanation.surface: A reality-TV contestant coming second in the final showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment of truth is a decisive test or crisis point, like a showdown.

clue.text: Travelling costumes in stretch cases

parts.note: a stretch is a space or expanse
legal cases are suits

explanation.surface: Clothes for a trip packed in stretchy luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests luggage, but it is lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacesuits are the outfits astronauts wear when travelling beyond Earth.

clue.text: Something fruity about naughty nude swinger

indicators.note: the fruit wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters of nude are disordered

explanation.surface: A saucy tale of a naked swinger with something fruity about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' tempts a racy reading, but it means anything that swings to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is a weight that swings to and fro, as in a clock.

clue.text: Uplifting pianos in Ultravox's gripping concert

indicators.note: Uplifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
the phrase grips the answer's letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Uplifting piano playing in an Ultravox concert holds the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'gripping concert' as the definition, leaving no hidden indicator; 'gripping' is that indicator, and 'concert' alone defines the answer. 'Uplifting' reverses NOSINU.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together in agreement, which is acting in unison.

clue.text: Aristocrat reckoning to share time with Hardy's girl

indicators.note: the two pieces share one letter for time, so one copy of it is dropped

parts.note: to count is to reckon
Tess of the d'Urbervilles, heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel

explanation.surface: A noblewoman sharing her time with Thomas Hardy's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share time with' means COUNT and TESS overlap on one T (the time abbreviation).
explanation.definitionFit: A countess is a noblewoman of the rank of earl or count, so an aristocrat.

clue.text: Worried, not getting a hi-tech acknowledgement

indicators.note: the word for worried does without the letter a

parts.note: to have cared is to have been worried
IT, information technology, is hi-tech

explanation.surface: Someone anxious that their hi-tech work goes unrecognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not getting a' removes A from CARED, giving CRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is public recognition for work done, as in film credits.

clue.text: Section of hose clip secures sunshade?

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clamp on a garden hose holding a parasol in place.
explanation.definitionFit: In an eclipse the moon blocks the sun, shading it as a parasol would; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Four male cooks creating recipes

indicators.note: to cook the books is to doctor them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Four men in the kitchen inventing dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' looks like a noun but is the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Formulae are set methods or prescriptions, sets of ingredients and steps like recipes.

clue.text: Amateur European rose in several bands?

parts.note: lay means non-professional, as in a lay preacher
rose is a pinkish red colour

explanation.surface: A European amateur gardener's rose growing in several stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests music groups; the question mark hints it means strata.
explanation.definitionFit: Something layered is arranged in strata, so it lies in several bands.

clue.text: Religious warriors that may be represented as manly aviators

indicators.note: the letters of manly aviators can be presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A religious troop of soldiers pictured as macho pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army is a Christian charity organised on military lines, its members soldiers of faith.

clue.text: Free biscuit served up off and on with more frosting

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters are presented going upwards
every other letter is taken, skipping one and keeping the next

explanation.surface: A free biscuit offered now and again with extra icing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off and on' takes alternate letters R E I C I from FREE BISCUIT; 'served up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier means frostier, coated with more ice or frost.

clue.text: See final part of 'Apocalypse Rising'

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read from bottom to top
the last four letters of the word Apocalypse are taken

explanation.surface: A film-fan reminder to watch the end of Apocalypse Rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns YPSE upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to see.

clue.text: Urchin regularly downed fried chips — 'veg' would be inaccurate

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or urchin

indicators.note: the letters at regular intervals, every second one, are kept

explanation.surface: A street urchin wolfed down fried chips calling them vegetables, which would not be accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' keeps the even letters R E C I S E of FRIED CHIPS VEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise means lacking exactness, so not accurate.

clue.text: Perhaps Jack's getting marching orders?

definitions.meaning: being given your ... means being sacked

explanation.surface: Jack is getting the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain to 'get your cards' is to be dismissed from a job, from the employment documents once handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacks are court cards in a pack, and being handed one's cards means dismissal from work.

clue.text: Drop something in the garden

definitions.meaning: to cast off, as a snake drops its skin
a hut for tools in the garden

explanation.surface: Letting something fall among the flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off or let fall, and a garden shed is a hut for storing tools.

clue.text: Contemporary Christmas?

definitions.meaning: the day of giving gifts, read as gift plus day

explanation.surface: Christmas as it is celebrated nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Present-day means modern; Christmas, whimsically, is the day for gifts.
